# secopsctl alerts

Manage SIEM detection alerts: list, get, enrich, AI investigate, and guarded feedback update

## alerts enrich

Read-only: show a SIEM alert's full context (rule detection, UDM events, entities, triage)

```text
secopsctl alerts enrich <alert-id>
```

```text
Fetch the rich per-alert view the console renders when an analyst opens an
alert — the rule detection(s), every mapped UDM event, the involved entities
and indicators (hosts, users, process hashes, domains), the alert's MITRE
tags, its SOAR case linkage, and the AI triage verdict when an agent has run.
--json prints the complete collection. The AI agent's investigation detail is
`alerts investigate <id> --latest`.
```

## alerts get

Get one alert by id (resolves its SOAR case id when the alert is cased)

```text
secopsctl alerts get <alert-id> [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--detections` | bool | false | include detection details (in --json) |

## alerts list

List alerts over a time window (snapshot view)

```text
secopsctl alerts list [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--filter` | string | - | server-side snapshot filter (default: feedback_summary.status != "CLOSED") |
| `--from` | string | - | explicit start (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); overrides --hours |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours when --from is not given |
| `--limit` | int | 100 | max alerts to return (0 = server default) |
| `--sort` | string | - | client-side sort: priority (worst first) \| created (newest first) |
| `--to` | string | - | explicit end (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); default now |

## alerts update

MUTATING (guarded): set triage feedback on one or more alerts

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl alerts update [<alert-id>...] [flags]
```

```text
Set alert feedback — the SIEM-side disposition: status, verdict, priority,
reason, reputation, scores, comment, root cause. Enum flags accept short
lower-case values (closed, false-positive, high, not-malicious, …) or the
full wire tokens. Apply the same update to many alerts in one guarded,
reviewable command: pass ids as arguments, resolve a known false-positive
burst with --where <snapshot-filter>, or stream ids on stdin with --stdin-ids
(the resolved set is listed before the guard). Guarded: dry-run by default,
--yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--comment` | string | - | analyst comment (an explicit empty string clears it) |
| `--confidence` | int | 0 | confidence score 0-100 |
| `--disregarded` | bool | false | mark the alert disregarded (=false to clear) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | --where: look-back window in hours for resolving ids |
| `--limit` | int | 1000 | --where: max alerts to resolve (a larger burst is reported, not silently dropped) |
| `--priority` | string | - | alert priority: info \| low \| medium \| high \| critical |
| `--reason` | string | - | close reason: not-malicious \| malicious \| maintenance |
| `--reputation` | string | - | alert reputation: useful \| not-useful |
| `--risk-score` | int | 0 | risk score 0-100 |
| `--root-cause` | string | - | root cause (an explicit empty string clears it) |
| `--severity` | int | 0 | severity score 0-100 |
| `--status` | string | - | alert status: new \| reviewed \| closed \| open |
| `--stdin-ids` | bool | false | read additional alert ids from stdin, one per line (# / blank lines skipped) |
| `--verdict` | string | - | alert verdict: true-positive \| false-positive |
| `--where` | string | - | resolve target alert ids from a server-side snapshot filter (a known FP burst) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

**Examples**

```bash
# close a false-positive burst matching a filter, reviewed first
  secopsctl alerts update --where 'detection.rule_name="Noisy Rule"' \
      --status closed --verdict false-positive --reason not-malicious

  # ids from a pipeline
  secopsctl alerts list --json | jq -r '.[].id' | \
    secopsctl alerts update --stdin-ids --status reviewed
```
